chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Zurarah and Muhammad, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

If the sun was completely eclipsed and burned over, and you did not know, then later came to know of that, then the qada' is upon you. But if it did not burn over completely, then there is no qada' upon you. And this detail does not contradict.

key_terms.احْتَرَقَتْ: was fully covered or intensely darkened in the context of the eclipse
key_terms.التَّفْصِيلَ: the legal distinction or detailed differentiation in the ruling
key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: making up a missed obligatory prayer after its time

ai.seo_question: If someone misses salat al-kusuf without knowing about a solar eclipse, must it be made up later?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about making up salat for a solar eclipse missed due to lack of knowledge. If the eclipse was total, qada' is required after one learns of it; if it was partial, no qada' is due.
